# flaky-tests-demo

The experiment from [Flaky tests: root causes, not retries](https://www.reticle.sh/blog/flaky-tests-root-causes-and-how-to-fix-them).

A tiny checkout page whose payment API answers after a random 200 to 1,400 ms, and two Playwright
tests of the same checkout:

- `tests/before.spec.ts` sleeps 1000 ms, checks the spinner is gone, and takes a screenshot.
- `tests/after.spec.ts` waits for the `/api/charge` response, checks it returned 200, then reads the
  order back and checks it is `paid`.

## Run it

Node 18 or later.

```bash
npm install
npm run demo
```

`demo` installs Chromium for Playwright, records a screenshot baseline for your machine, then runs
each test 20 times on the same code.

Expect `before` to fail on some runs, whenever the charge takes longer than the 1000 ms sleep. The
latency is random, so the count changes every time: on macOS with Node 22 we got 8 failures of 20 in
the run printed in the post, and 3 of 20 on a later run. `after` passed 20 of 20 both times.

## Files

- `server.mjs`: the fixture shop (no dependencies).
- `tests/`: the two tests, exactly as printed in the post.
- `playwright.config.ts`: starts the server; keeps one screenshot baseline per machine.
